HOW WEAPONS ATTACH:
- Enemy weapons are rig 'items' with their own image: grip (item px), hand (figure px), parent part, rest angle, z, tip, scale (snapped to the pixel grid by item_factor), hp, disables, recolor, bow. RigLibrary.item_rest is rest*hand*scale*-grip. RigRenderer._solve chains parent_world*hand*rest*scale*-grip (rig_renderer.gd:1663-1670), and poses move them through pose.items[id].
- Alternatively the weapon is drawn into the figure as a part with a 'tip': item_parts:true, or Hell layered rigs, where RigPoses._layered_extras turns item motion into part motion.
- Hero weapons are not rig items. hero_look draws them (draw_hero passes with_items=false, rig_renderer.gd:534) and has its own drop physics.

HANDOVER BETWEEN HIT, PART LOSS, DEATH AND RAGDOLL (story worlds):
(1) The host's hit test aims a part: drake_rig.shot_hits/swing_hits/blast_hits against the transforms last drawn (renderer.part_transforms), with the rest pose as fallback.
(2) _damage_mob calls take_aim, then damage, then BodyParts.damage (the full amount counts against total HP). A part at 0 HP is lost, together with its also_detach parts. A vital part kills.
(3) DrakeRigHost._sever queues EVENT_SEVER (stagger, flash, palette, sounds). hell_game._route_rig_events turns it into hitstop, sound, shake and a burst.
(4) In the next frame, frame() puts a snapshot with lost[] into renderer.observe. A newly lost id calls _detach, which builds a debris piece from that part's last drawn transform, plus chips.
(5) Death: hell_monsters makes a corpse {uid, kill=_kill_fx (blow dir, tier, element), tumble} and calls bind_world(g.box_blocked). The host passes dying_p, and RigRenderer._start_death runs the family rule (ragdoll_all, shed list, burst). _piece gives each part a velocity from the blow, a z-lift, spin and the element look. A held item flies off to its hand's side.
(6) _step_debris integrates gravity, bounces, solid() walls, friction, rest, a shove between pieces, a cap and dither crumble.

All of this is visual. The ragdoll never feeds back into gameplay and is separate from story_wreck's debris physics and from the hero weapon's drop physics.

Gaps:
- The Frostgruft path (FrostRigs) skips steps 1-4 (no part loss), sends no kill direction and has no walls.
- Companions use BodyParts with the rest-pose part_near and share story_hero's renderer, which has no walls.

notes:
Read-only survey, 2026-11-01, branch codex_v2 (origin/main == codex_v2 == b178a185). Files were being edited by another workflow while I read: hell_game.gd moved by ~4 lines between reads (_update_camera 3428 -> 3432, _process 2388 -> 2382), so later hell_game line numbers can be off by a few. The _ready wiring lines (322-493) stayed the same.

How I counted reach-ins: a regex classifier over `g.`/`game.` (read / write / call / signal). Calls like g.get("x") count as calls, but they are really duck-typed reads. I left out false positives where `g` is a local variable (world_core.gd, world_pack.gd, pool_paint.gd, umlaut_caps.gd) and 'e.g.' in comments (music.gd). No module uses signals toward the host. The only signal wiring is host-side (pause_menu, inventory_panel, options_panel).

Main findings:
1. Three kinds of module exist today. (a) Real modules with no host reach: world kit, story_camera, sfx/audio_mix/music, feedback.gd, item_rules, save_store, the HUD kit. (b) A duck-typed contract: inventory.gd against a 'crypt game' that both game.gd and story_items.gd imitate. (c) Story adapters with 90 to 135 reaches each: story_feel 90, story_glow 118, story_items 135, story_sound 43.
2. The cores are already shared between the old dungeon and the story worlds (feedback, sfx, music, HUD kit, inventory). The coupling sits almost entirely in the story_* adapters and in hell_game.gd as a service locator: 27 modules, about 2256 reaches.
3. The fixes that come up again and again are all host-side. Build one per-frame snapshot. Use a WorldContext with public combat and query methods instead of the private g._* calls. Add a world_id theme key, which replaces three string-sniffing rules (story_save.gd:13-17, main_menu.gd:519-525, story_sound.gd:93-96). Use one settings path (4 copies) and one JSON cache per file. 92 JSON.parse_string calls sit in 66 src files, with no shared loader.
4. The app root is still src/main.tscn -> src/game.gd. It opens the story scenes and resumes saves by their stored scene path (game.gd:2309, 2734-2750). So the old game must stay compiling and loadable, and moving the story scenes would break existing saves.
5. Suggested order, cheapest first: world kit README and accessor (S); camera values into JSON (S); UI kit cleanup plus committing umlaut_caps (S); saves world_id and single carry list (S); feedback hold() and particles() facade (S); written ItemHost contract (M); then the adapters (L), starting with story_sound because the host already ticks most of its inputs.

Workflow risks:
- Uncommitted local edits are sitting in saidPC's world-kit files (a difficulty curve in GD, JS and the three packs).
- Line endings are mixed in the working tree, and .gitattributes has no *.gd rule.
- There is no CI or test runner. Commit 51066c11 records 10 suites that already fail on main.

notes:
Answer to the user's question: yes, this is possible. The talent runtime is the best candidate, because it already has an implicit host contract with two implementations (src/game.gd crypt and src/hell/hell_talents.gd story worlds). The work is to write that contract down as a SpellHost base class and to remove the duck typing. A good model is the brother's world_kit (src/world_kit/world_core.gd + world_pack.gd, data-only worlds, tools/world_kit/README.md, tests/world_kit_parity_test.gd): a 'Zauber-Baukasten' would be a spell core + type handlers + data-only spells + parity tests.

How a spell is described today. It is neither a pure cast->travel->impact->residue description nor code per spell; it is code per TYPE. Every talent's numbers are data in talents.json (168 talents, 12 specs x 14). Its behaviour is one of 28 coded types in talent_combat._run (358-638); 15 of them serve exactly one talent and 1 ('wall') serves none. The four beats exist only in the look (talent_fx: gather/shot/impact/residue, driven by element = id prefix and tier = vfx_talents.json). The impact is guessed from vanished shots, and 29 lines of per-id special cases plus a match by id in talent_ults sit on top.

How to add a spell today:
(a) Existing type, default look: 1 file. Add a talents.json entry plus its id in classes.<cls>.specs[].talents, using an existing icon motif. Sound comes automatically via audio_rules.json cast_by_type/events. Optional: tier in vfx_talents.json. The id must be '<spec>_<n>', because the element and spec are parsed from the prefix in 6+ places.
(b) A new behaviour or its own look: about 8-11 files. talents.json, talent_combat.gd (new _run branch, maybe step/zones), hell_talents.gd and/or game.gd if a new host service is needed, talent_fx.gd (id branch), talent_pixels.gd (shape), vfx_talents.json, talent_ults.gd for an ultimate, story_sound.gd + audio_rules/audio_sfx.json for a new event kind, src/ui/talent_icons.gd (icons are ASCII motifs in code), docs. Evidence: commit ebc94c65 (Flammenmeer, Pyro-Monster, signature ultimates) touched about 25 src files.
(c) An armour power: armor_powers.json + 5 match blocks in armor_powers.gd + items.json + an icon.
